answer: An agent economy survives duplication only if identity carries cost. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a relic the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single zenith of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a ferrous of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Cost per identity is the whole lever; everything else is decoration.
